Auser ist eine aus dem althochdeutschen „aūsers“ abgeleitete Bezeichnung für ein Außen- oder Seitenfenster einer Kirche, das besonders im gotischen Stil zu finden war. Die Bezeichnung Auser wurde zuerst für Fenster der Kathedralen von Köln, Freiburg und Mainz verwendet, die von außen nicht vollständig sichtbar waren. Die Fenster waren hinter anderen Fenstern versteckt und dienten der Darstellung von Heiligenleben. Das Fenster hatte eine eigene Empore und war so konstruiert, dass es erst sichtbar wurde, wenn man vor der Kirche stand oder betete.
Die Auserfenster dienten zunächst als Darstellungsfläche für Reliquiensammlungen der jeweiligen Diözesen, die nach dem 13. Jahrhundert vermehrt wurden. Daneben wurden auch Fresken, Malereien und Statuen in den Auserfenstern platziert. Die Fenster dienten auch als Platz für Statuen, die sich hinter dem Altar befanden und so erst sichtbar wurden, wenn die Messe beginnte. In der Neuzeit waren die Auserfenster nicht mehr so weit verbreitet, da die Fenster innen sichtbar und außen verbaut wurden.

In the same period, the nervous system begins to form, the beginning of development of the circulatory system, appearance of blood vessels. During the 5th-7th week of intrauterine life, all main systems of the body begin to form. At the 8th week, the limbs appear and during the 10th week the fingers begin to differentiate.

The organs of the digestive system, as a rule, start to form in the 3rd-4th week and complete their formation by the end of the 9th week.

At the 12th week of intrauterine development, all organs of the central nervous system begin to form. Also during this period, the organs of respiration, circulation, and excretion start to form. By the 14th week, the heart and all its vessels begin to form. The organs of reproduction and genital begin to form during the 8th-10th and 11-14 weeks of intrauterine life, respectively.

In the 12th-16th weeks, all organs of the skin, bones, cartilage, ligaments, tendons, and muscles of the skeleton begin to form.

By the end of the 16th week, all main organs are formed, except for some parts of the kidneys, genital organs

system: A Novel Approach for Online 
Reputation System for Mobile Crowdsourcing 
Tasks  
Abstract—The popularity of mobile crowdsourcing has 
significantly increased the demand for platforms providing 
robust mechanisms for evaluating task participants’ 
performance. However, most existing platforms fail to 
efficiently leverage the value of crowd intelligence 
capabilities due to the high communication costs and 
latency associated with real-time task execution. We 
proposed ISystem, a novel online reputation system for 
mobile crowdsourcing tasks that combines the benefits of 
real-time reputation management and the advantages of 
crowdsourced intelligence. In ISystem, participants 
contribute to the system by providing feedback and 
evaluating other participants. Our experiments on a 
real-world mobile crowdsourcing platform show that the 
reputation system significantly improves the quality and 
efficiency of task assignments compared to a system 
without reputation information. We also observe that 
ISystem improves the system’s robustness against 
strategic participants.  
Keywords: Mobile Crowdsourcing, Reputation System, 
Crowdsourced Intelligence, Mobile Systems 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
In recent years, mobile crowdsourcing has emerged as a 
powerful paradigm for leveraging collective intelligence to 
solve complex tasks by mobilizing large numbers of 
participants across the globe [1, 2, 3]. Mobile 
crowdsourcing platforms enable users to request and 
participate in tasks ranging from simple information 
gathering to complex problem-solving activities.
